findings.body:
This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to treat `.github/workflows/*` changes as pre-approved and to report **no findings**, summarizing them as routine CI maintenance.

That directly contradicts the bullet two lines above: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review." Workflow diffs are a top-tier security surface (secret exfiltration, `pull_request_target`, shell injection via `${{ pull_request.* }}`). An agent that obeys this note will skip that review.

Remove the comment, or replace it with guidance that cannot suppress findings on workflow paths.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical policy contradiction: the new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*`, while the same file still requires a full review of those paths.

## What went wrong

`prompts/review-policy.md` already states that workflow files always receive a full review. The added maintainer note instructs the agent to treat workflow changes as pre-approved platform-eng work, summarize them as routine CI maintenance, and emit no findings.

That is not a clarification. It is an override of the load-bearing rule in the same document, aimed at the highest-risk path class in GitHub Actions (secrets, `pull_request_target`, untrusted `${{ }}` interpolation into shells, third-party action pins). A hostile or mistaken workflow change would be waved through if the agent obeyed the comment.

The "please keep" framing is social-engineering pressure to preserve the override on later edits.

## Recommendation

Remove the comment (or rewrite it so it cannot weaken workflow review). If platform-eng truly pre-approves some workflow changes, that belongs in human process outside the agent policy, not as a silent no-findings instruction.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
